title: Shrink a refused crane booking to its core

blocks.text: A transmission utility books one mobile crane for its substation lifts. A scheduling check, `fits(lifts)`, answers whether a set of lifts can all be booked in one month (it is given, and its inside does not matter here). When a month's set is refused, the planning master needs a no-good cut: "not all of these lifts in this month". The fewer lifts the cut names, the more plans it rules out, so the planners want the refused set shrunk to a **core**: a subset that `fits` still refuses, from which no single lift can be dropped without `fits` accepting the rest.

Write first what the cut on a core $`S`$ says in the master's variables $`x_{l,m}`$ (lift $`l`$ in month $`m`$), and why it is valid for every plan. Then write `shrink(lifts, fits)` to return a core of the refused list `lifts`, as a list in the input's order. Try each lift once, in order.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable


def shrink(lifts: list[str], fits: Callable[[list[str]], bool]) -> list[str]:
    """A core of a refused set: still refused, and no lift can be dropped from it."""
    # TODO: write what the cut on a core says first, then shrink the list.
    return []


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(shrink(["a", "b", "c"], lambda s: not {"a", "c"} <= set(s)))
